reading: Grades as in apps/dielines/docs/research/STANDARDS.md: P primary, C converter, G generator, S search excerpt only, X our own reasoning. provisional: true marks any value the web did not settle; it prints as ⟪PROVISIONAL⟫ and a folded sample decides it. Source ids are in ../sources.md.

outside_gain_per_crease.why: FEFCO Rec. 101: inside = crease centres − one thickness for length and breadth, so half a caliper per crease; the outside is its mirror

fit_gap_mm.why: a panel end stops this short of the surface it meets, so board and folding tolerance cannot make it collide; inside the owner's 0.0–0.5 mm bar

slot_play_mm.why: a slot's width is the plies through it plus this. Makers on the laser cut cardboard tighter than the board; a steel rule die is not a laser, so we keep 1.0's play until a sample says otherwise

slot_end_play_mm.why: a slot's length is the tab plus this at each end

cut_to_crease_mm.why: at least two calipers and 3 mm between a cut and a parallel crease: Cito traces cracking to a crease with too little room; the number is ours

min_panel_calipers.why: the narrowest panel between two parallel creases, and at least 3 mm: Cito's double crease starts at 3 mm centres

web_calipers.why: the board left between an opening and a free edge: 1.0's rule; the house's own inserts use 8.5–9 mm

clearance_total_mm.why: the owner: product + 1 mm; the web gave no number for corrugated decks (research: not found)

max_lean_deg.why: the most a product may lean in its opening: sets how deep the deck holds it, depth = clearance ÷ tan(lean)

floor_tab_w_mm.why: a tab into the floor or an inner wall

tab_radius_mm.why: a tab's free corners rounded: research placeholder, ≥ 1.5 mm

barb_overhang_mm.why: a barbed tongue's head, past its neck each side: it flexes through once and catches under the board. No source gave a number

tongue_head_mm.why: a header tongue's head, under the slot

tongue_taper_mm.why: the lead-in that finds the slot

flap_w_mm.why: a side wall's corner flap trapped between a double wall's leaves (US10144549 traps its tabs the same way); 1.0's flap width

cap_calipers.why: the rim of a rolled double wall (US10159361 rolls its walls over; Cito's double crease spans 3–8 mm)

half_cut_depth.why: a 180° fold on the header's top: a partial cut from the unprinted side, so the printed liner is the hinge. One patent's range, excerpt only

perf_cut_mm.why: a tear line's cut. Label-industry patterns only (0.5–2 mm ties); the corrugated 3×3 and 6×6 patterns were not found

header_tall_ratio.why: a header standing free above the tray taller than this takes a back-brace. No source gave a limit

brace_foot_mm.why: how far a back-brace stands behind the tray

face_bar_cap_plus_mm.why: the owner's 'every product's front face': the whole cap and this much of the shade below it, from each eye, across the product's whole width. A full face on the rear rows would need a rise of a whole product per row

shade_window_share.why: the owner's shade rule, 2026-10-31: every shade shows its colour; at least half of each product's colour window seen from the shopper's eye, or on the flat tray, its tester's

face_bar_min_mm.why: the bar for a product with no cap: 1.0's top band

header_share_of_product.why: a header's height when the brief gives none: 1.0's rule. Published proportion: none found; one catalogue listing shows about 0.32 of its fixture

ect_e_flute_kn_m.why: ECT 32 lb/in, a common grade (board maker's certificate example); the mill's figure replaces it

mckee_constant.why: BCT = 5.87 × ECT × √(perimeter × caliper), N, N/mm, mm

humid_loss_80rh.why: box compression lost at 80 % RH (FBA table, via Georgia Tech)

product_mass_g.why: a filled product when the brief gives no weight

max_steps.why: assembly steps, one person, no tools, no glue

cf2_types_note: CF2 1 cut, 2 crease, 3 perforation, 4 score (Kodak's table, excerpt, C12). No half-cut code was found: half-cuts go out as 4 and a shop can remap them.
